Healthcare | U.S. Representative Scott Franklin American families should be free to make healthcare decisions that fit their specific needs. Our healthcare requires market-based solutions, not a one-size fits all approach that reduces options, increases cost and impacts timely and affordable care. Healthcare decisions are best made by you and your doctor, not by Congress and unelected Washington bureaucrats.</p> <p>Expanding access to health savings accounts (HSAs), will enable individuals to set aside pre-tax dollars for their health care costs and the services and products HSAs typically cover. Congress should also address expanding telehealth services to broaden healthcare access for millions of families.</p> <p>Congress must also ensure Medicare continues to deliver for older Americans who depend on it. That means ensuring seniors have access and choices to receive the health care they need, including lower prescription drug costs and affordable premiums for Medicare health plan options.</p>" /> Skip to Content Healthcare Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email American families should be free to make healthcare decisions that fit their specific needs. Our healthcare requires market-based solutions, not a one-size fits all approach that reduces options, increases cost and impacts timely and affordable care. Healthcare decisions are best made by you and your doctor, not by Congress and unelected Washington bureaucrats. Expanding access to health savings accounts (HSAs), will enable individuals to set aside pre-tax dollars for their health care costs and the services and products HSAs typically cover. Congress should also address expanding telehealth services to broaden healthcare access for millions of families. Congress must also ensure Medicare continues to deliver for older Americans who depend on it. That means ensuring seniors have access and choices to receive the health care they need, including lower prescription drug costs and affordable premiums for Medicare health plan options. Agriculture | U.S. Representative Scott Franklin Florida’s 18<sup>th</sup> Congressional District includes the Heartland of Florida.&nbsp; It starts north in Polk County at I-4 and stretches down past Lake Okeechobee, nearly to the Everglades.&nbsp; Home to over 200 specialty crops and most of Florida’s citrus and cattle operations, I’m proud to represent the largest agriculture district east of the Mississippi.</p> <p>After my first term in Congress, I worked to secure a seat on the House Appropriations Committee, where I am on the Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration. &nbsp;In this role, I’m fighting for Florida’s agriculture priorities. &nbsp;Agriculture is a vital part of our Florida economy and the lifeblood of many of our rural communities. &nbsp;Our farmers, ranchers, growers and producers not only feed the nation and the world, but also create thousands of jobs that strengthen our local economy.</p> <p>Florida’s citrus industry plays a critical role in our state’s economy and FL-18 contains 70% of Florida’s citrus production. &nbsp;Unfortunately, unfair trade imbalances, invasive diseases and hurricanes have taken a toll on the industry. &nbsp;Some growers have been forced to sell their lands for development because they cannot overcome continued challenges.</p> <p>That’s why I introduced legislation to bring needed relief to our agriculture producers and protect our citrus industry including:</p> <ul> <li><a>H.R. 662</a>, the Block Grant Assistance Act – This bill ensures the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) can provide needed relief to agriculture producers devastated by Hurricanes Ian and Nicole. &nbsp;It gives the Agriculture Secretary needed authority to provide block grants to Florida to assist producers affected by recent hurricanes.&nbsp; As a devout Christian, I will continue to fight for religious freedom for every American. I will also continue to support basic Judeo-Christian values such as protecting human life. Congress has a sacred duty to speak up for those who can’t speak for themselves. As a father and staunch defender of the unborn, I will continue every effort to defend life and speak on behalf of the voiceless. National Security/Defense | U.S. Representative Scott Franklin Florida has 20 major military installations, including three of ten Unified Combatant Commands:&nbsp; U.S. Central Command, U.S. Southern Command, and U.S. Special Operations Command.&nbsp; Additionally, over 69,000 active-duty personnel, 205,000 military retirees, and 1.5 million veterans call Florida home.</p> <p>As a retired Naval aviator who deployed in several global conflicts and sat on the House Armed Services Committee, I understand the challenges facing our men and women in uniform, as well as what is required to keep our country safe.</p> <p>Now more than ever, America’s leadership in the world is critical. We are in an era of Great Power Competition with China and Russia, coupled with threats from rogue regimes in Iran and North Korea. We must provide the necessary resources to ensure we have the best equipped and most lethal fighting force on the globe. Our military solely exists to provide for our common defense by being prepared to fight and win wars, if called upon to do so. Our service members should never be used for social experiments or to advance a political agenda.</p> <p>As a member of the Armed Services Committee in my first term, I secured several key provisions in the Fiscal Years 2022 and 2023 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). These provisions include:</p> <ul> <li>Providing congressional oversight of the Afghanistan Withdrawal</li> <li>Supporting small businesses working in the artificial intelligence sector</li> <li>Enhancing the Department of Defense’s cybersecurity</li> <li>Modernizing our fighting force</li> <li>Funding the new KC-46 refueling tanker program</li> </ul> <p>In the 118<sup>th</sup> Congress, I now serve on the House Appropriations Committee. In this capacity, I will continue to support a strong military well-equipped to face the challenges of the 21<sup>st</sup> century. I will also work to ensure fiscal discipline when national security and defense spending priorities come to the full committee and House floor for a vote.</p>" /> Skip to Content National Security/D

Energy | U.S. Representative Scott Franklin America is a country blessed with rich natural resources and emerging technologies that must be developed in an environmentally sound manner that is sustainable for future generations. That’s why developing an all-of-the-above energy strategy that meets our short and long-term plans for achieving energy independence is critical.</p> <p>When President Biden took office, America had achieved energy independence. Sadly, he chose to cancel the Keystone XL pipeline, release millions of barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) and block federal oil and gas leasing, which has contributed to record-high prices at the pump.</p> <p>That’s why my House colleagues and I passed H.R. 1,<i> the Lower Energy Costs Act</i>. This bill will fast-track domestic energy production, expedite construction of critical infrastructure projects through permitting reforms and ensure that critical minerals needed for advanced technologies come from America – not China. I also voted for H.R. 21, <i>the Strategic Production Response Act, </i>which<i> </i>would prevent the president from tapping the SPR for political purposes and require the Biden administration to create a plan to refill it.</p> <p>Ensuring America becomes energy independent again is critical now more than ever. We must be committed to finding common sense solutions to meet our energy needs and invest in domestic energy sources that will support new jobs and growth for the 21<sup>st</sup> century.</p>" /> Skip to Content Energy Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email America is a country blessed with rich natural resources and emerging technologies that must be developed in an environmentally sound manner that is sustainable for future generations.
